title: A Two-Track Property Stabilization
gist: Gavekal Dragonomics says housing prices in China's four Tier 1 cities have stabilized and partly rebounded, but oversupply elsewhere means the national market will diverge rather than follow. (Paywalled excerpt only.)

insights.claim: Prices of new and existing housing in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen have stabilized and even rebounded somewhat in recent months, signalling an end to the decline is in sight for that corner of the market.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Tier 1 cities have long led the national market, so this is an early positive signal for China property sentiment.

insights.claim: Other Chinese cities overbuilt more and have less sticky demand than Tier 1 cities, so their housing prices will face oversupply pressure for years and the Tier 1 turning point is unlikely to spread.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Expect widening price divergence; avoid extrapolating Tier 1 stabilization to lower-tier exposure.
insights.quote: an ever-wider divergence in prices and performance
